title: Hikerdelic Egg Chaser Rugby Shirt Mushroom
body_html:
Rugby isn’t a sport you’d associate with the usual down-to-earth vibes we identify here at Hikerdelic, but then this is just a rugby shirt in name only. We don’t expect you to be wearing it as you roll about in the mud.

We wanted to nod to the heritage of the rugby shirt while still making it clear it’s not an actual shirt for rugby and all it entails. And so, the Egg Chaser Rugby Shirt was born.

This multi-stripe version takes all the good bits you find on a traditional rugby shirt, and removes the bits we didn’t fancy. The rugged, stiff, thick cotton fabric is replaced by a meticulously chosen loopback jersey fabric, with stripes embedded within. It creates a more comfortable garment that feels more like a really posh lightweight sweatshirt. 

Colour-wise, we’ve gone full-on liquorice allsorts with this colourway and the other one that shares this pattern, without really meaning to. These autumnal colours will work way beyond your conker-collecting escapades. Collar and cuff-wise, you’ll be please with what you find, while branding is subtle, via our increasingly familiar green side tab which appears on the left hip, adding a pop of colour.

These are a pretty regular fit, so it’s best you buy the size you wear in most of your other clothing.

title: Hikerdelic x Elliker Semer Sling Bag Navy
body_html:
Created by our friends at ELLIKER the Semer Sling Bag is proof that the smallest bits of kit are often the ones you end up relying on most. Built for festivals, day walks, train station scrambles and aimless city wandering alike, this compact 1L crossbody keeps the essentials close without weighing you down or getting in the way.

Constructed on our suggestion from durable diamond ripstop nylon alongside recycled polyester with a waterproof PU coating, the Semer is designed to handle changeable weather, accidental downpours and the general unpredictability of everyday life. A PFC/PFAS-free water-repellent finish adds an extra layer of protection while keeping things environmentally considered, which feels only right for something intended to spend plenty of time outdoors.

The main compartment is secured via a waterproof YKK zip, with additional front and rear zipped pockets giving easy access to the stuff you always seem to need in a hurry. Inside, things stay satisfyingly organised thanks to mesh slip compartments, an internal zipped pocket and a built-in key clip that should hopefully reduce the chances of that all-too-familiar pocket panic.

Daisy chain webbing across the front allows for modular attachment options, while the structured base helps the bag sit comfortably against the body whether worn crossbody or carried by the grab handle.

Minimal in size but properly functional where it counts, the Semer continues the shared approach between Hikerdelic and ELLIKER: useful gear, built with purpose, ready for almost everywhere.

title: Hikerdelic x Elliker Cautley Flap Over Backpack Green
body_html:
Built together with our pals across the Pennines at ELLIKER the Cautley Backpack is a 23L daypack designed for people who refuse to see much distinction between the daily commute and disappearing off into the hills for a few hours. Technical enough for proper outdoor use, but without looking like you’re about to summit K2 on your lunch break, it’s a bag made for modern wandering in all its various forms.

Constructed from durable nylon ripstop with weather-resistant finishes alongside recycled polyester with a waterproof PU coating, the Cautley is built to deal with unpredictable forecasts, overpacked train journeys and whatever else the day decides to throw at you. The flap-over top comes secured with adjustable clip fastenings and carabiner anchors, while a waterproof YKK zip entry gives quick access to the main compartment without the usual rummaging about.

Storage-wise, there’s plenty going on without it becoming overcomplicated. An external padded side sleeve fits up to a 15” laptop (16” MacBook friendly for the tech-heads amongst us), complete with slip pockets for phones and pens, while inside you’ll find additional organisation via elasticated compartments, zipped storage, key clip attachments and modular daisy chain webbing.

Externally, expandable bottle pockets, adjustable elasticated cradles and multiple attachment points mean there’s room for extra layers, water bottles and all the miscellaneous gear you somehow convince yourself you’ll definitely need.

Comfort comes courtesy of padded ergonomic shoulder straps, a breathable back panel and adjustable chest and waist straps that keep everything feeling stable whether you’re weaving through city crowds or heading somewhere with significantly more sheep than people.

Like all our favourite bits of gear, the Cautley sits happily somewhere between functional outdoor equipment and everyday essential. Designed with ELLIKER’s technical expertise and viewed through a Hikerdelic lens, it’s ready for almost everywhere.

title: Proper Magazine Issue 50 - Anglesey Cover
body_html:
The one you've all been waiting for. Twenty(ish) years in the making. What started as a fanzine printed on a £40 home printer has now, somehow, turned 50. As it's name suggests, this issue is a Celebration of everything that makes Proper, Proper.

Inside, you’ll find a guide to Manchester’s finest spots; the top 50 films of the last twenty years; a celebration of Kickers; Nigel Cabourn’s latest collaboration with Mammut; a deep dive into the fabric of Rab; a comparison between Alaska and Anglesey; and a colossal journey to Switzerland to photograph every jacket we could possibly squeeze into a suitcase.

It’s the culmination of years of graft, a handful of misprints, big ambitions and even bigger coats. We’re genuinely proud of this one, and we hope that you’ll feel it on every page.

Here's to 50 more.

title: Hikerdelic x Elliker Semer Sling Bag Black
body_html:
For those days when you need to travel light but still keep essentials about your person, the Semer Sling bag is your 1L pal. It may be small in size, but it'll still pack a punch.

Made from 100% recycled polyester with a PU waterproof coating, the Semer shrugs off light rain and daily splashes, keeping your gear dry while keeping things lightweight and low-key.

The adjustable strap lets you wear it your way, whether around the waist, cross-body or slung over one shoulder, with a quick-release clip so you can switch it up in seconds.

Up front, daisy-chain webbing gives you space to clip on extras, while YKK zips open into a front storage pocket and a rear compartment for easy-access stashing. Inside, you’ll find a key clip, a zip pocket pouch, and an extra daisy-chain strap to keep your setup locked and organised.

title: Hikerdelic x Elliker Cautley Flap Over Backpack Black
body_html:
The most substantial piece in our three-item capsule with Elliker comes our take on their Cautley Flap Over Backpack. This 23L capacity shape-shifter is built for big days and long weekends, whether embracing the outdoors or going down a more relaxed route.

Built from 100% recycled polyester with a waterproof PU coating, the Cautley keeps things light on your back and lighter on the planet, without compromising on toughness. 

The flap-over top locks down with an adjustable clip system and movable carabiner anchors, so you can shift and tweak the carry depending on what you’re hauling. Whether it’s overpacked or travelling light, this bag flexes with your load. A double-zip front access means you can grab essentials fast without that annoying rummaging around at the airport gate or out on your hike with freezing fingers..

Up top, a padded external laptop sleeve fits up to a 16” MacBook (other laptop brands will also fit, obvs), with built-in pockets for phone, pens and medical items such as your inhaler, while a zip pocket in the flap keeps your grab-and-go items close. On the outside, dual elasticated bottle pockets, adjustable side cradles and daisy-chain webbing give you plenty of ways to lash on extra kit.

Inside, the roomy drawstring main compartment hides another elasticated laptop sleeve, plus internal organisers and a zip pocket with key clip and daisy-chain strap to keep your setup dialled.

Finished with ergonomic padded straps, a breathable back panel, and adjustable waist and chest straps, the Cautley stays balanced and comfortable whether you’re weaving through city streets or heading off the beaten track.

Crafted from 100% recycled polyester with a tough PU waterproof coating, the Carston shrugs off the elements while keeping its footprint light. 

Up front and out back, daisy-chain webbing gives you space to clip on your gear and make it your own. And with a detachable crossbody strap, you can switch it up on the fly: wear it cross-body, sling it over your shoulder, or grab it by hand and go.

title: Hikerdelic Drifter Fleece Blue/Lime
body_html:
Everyone (ok, everyone who is a bit of a geek) knows fleece fabric was first developed in the 70s via a partnership between a certain Patagonia brand and Polartec. The idea was to create something synthetic that had the warmth properties of wool, but was also light and quick-drying. Fleece was born. Since then, it has found its way everywhere. No wardrobe is complete without some sort of fleece item and having done some pretty popular shaggy sherpa fleece items of our own over the last few years, this is our first foray into a more polarfleece arena. 

The Drifter Fleece comes in a choice of two colours. One inspired by the depths of autumn and one that takes its cue from late summer and early spring. They both do the same job and are both here in limited numbers, but which colour you elect to employ depends on your mood. 

These are a slightly boxy fit, designed for activity, albeit light activity, like perhaps out walking the dog, wandering around an area of outstanding natural beauty or just socialising with some exciteable friends. You know the ones.

title: Hikerdelic Bridestones LS T-shirt White
body_html:
Drinking in the rugged mystique of the Pennine landscape these lovely long-sleevers take inspiration from the mystical Bridestones, a cluster of weathered gritstone outcrops overlooking the Calder Valley.

They have long been a local landmark, inspiring walkers, climbers, and storytellers alike. Our design team wanted to pay collective tribute to this local landscape blending natural drama with cultural heritage, grounding the garment in a strong sense of place.

Folklore suggests wedding ceremonial were once performed here, with each participant standing atop a different stone. Others believe the site was sacred to the Celtic goddess Bridget, and the stones aided fertility. We love all that sort of stuff. 

Available in limited numbers across both a white and a black long sleeve version, these are the very essence of what Hikerdelic is.

title: Hikerdelic Worker Jacket Navy
body_html:
When we began to explore influences for Spring/Summer '23 we were drawn to the 1970s and the workwear donned by dutiful public servants here in the UK. Workwear has long since expanded into fashion, but the noble professions that provided employment for millions in the 70s on these isles feel under-represented. With that in mind we mainlined YouTube documentaries, marvelled at how much older than their age everyone dressed back then, and how cool the colour brown can look when worn the right way. 

Like the similar Plaid Worker Jacket, this Navy version takes the uniforms of yesteryear and combines corduroy with cotton, a clash of the past and the present. 

Whether it's the brutal late 70's borstal drama of Scum, or the much lighter prison tales of Porridge, the simplicity of a navy outfit was a great leveller, whether worn while paying back to society for crimes, or the altogether more wholesome jobs done by those in industry back then.   

We designed some matching trousers to go with this outfit, and while you're more than welcome to pair them up, we don't demand it. This Worker Jacket is a year-round essential that can be worn at the height of summer when something smart is called for, yet also as a mid-layer when the wind begins to whip up a storm.

Constructed from 100% cotton, this quintessentially British workwear piece flies the flag for a time when the UK was still powered by elbow grease and plain old hard work.

title: Proper Magazine Issue 47 - Geodome Cover
body_html:
Right you lot, we’re back – by neutrally popular demand – to present the 47th edition of our magazine. 

To be honest, we did have some concerns about this issue after reading a study from the American National Bureau of Economic Research, which claims that human misery peaks at age 47. 

Now, we’re not exactly sure if the mental state of a magazine aligns with the emotional patterns of a person (probably not), but given the timing of this study and the lack of vitamin D in the air this time of year, we weren’t about to take any risks. 

So, to save the magazine from hitting rock bottom, we’ve made a concerted effort to fill it with feel-good content. 

This feel-good material mostly comes from our conversations with true aficionados – passionate individuals obsessed with everything from clothing (obviously), to running, fishing, vintage stuff, interior design, writing, and more. 

Working with these aficionado’s has reminded us (not that we really needed it) that it's important to be wildly passionate about the stuff you’re into, even if people look at you a bit weird for it. Who’s arsed?  

In this issue we also reflect on the high points of what has been a pretty solid year for Proper, so it's got loads of stuff in it that we’re proud about. 

Jokes aside, I think everyone has done a fantastic job on this publication, and I hope that the passion, and effort that has gone into it comes across on every page.

So, what are you waiting for? Get stuck into it.

title: Proper Magazine Issue 37 - KEEN Cover
body_html:
Embracing the freedoms we've been deprived of for so long, Proper 37 explores the theme of ‘Escape’ It's a word that can be interpreted in a number of ways, which will become more and more apparent with each page you turn.

Whether it be a literal escape or simply a way to relieve the pressure of the daily grind, Proper have got it covered in this bumper issue which boasts a page count on the cusp of 200. Almost certainly their biggest yet. 

Brands you've heard of feature heavily alongside brands you may not be familiar with. They’ve even pitched lovely indoor homeware against impressive outdoor equipment and interviewed the main men at Gramicci, Kennedy Magazine, and more. 

Overall it's the best one yet and you'd be a fool to miss out.

title: Proper Magazine Issue 40 - Steep Cover
body_html:
For Proper Magazine’s variation on the midlife crisis, we’ve vowed to do one thing: shine a light on what the youth in our region are doing, and open ourselves up to the passage of time.

For starters, we’ve got an editorial by Royal Ragz, where the Manchester-based collector’s archive Patagonia SSTs, as well as other fishing-related gear, are shot at a quarry sight in Devon. 

There’s a brief psychedelic explosion from Oi Polloi’s latest sportswear range, and a look into the motivation behind Steep Learning Group, who’ve been active in the promotion of climbing as a democratic sport, as well as pioneering some of its more aesthetic elements.  

We’ve got a quick dive into the paintings of Kingston Poplar, a Retford-born painter who captures the quirks of contemporary life by honing in on some of its more peculiar elements.  

Over in our hometown of Stockport, there’s a bubbling record shop by the name of All Night Flight, which our very own Ryan Kimberley took a trip to. Ryan spoke to the owner, Tom Houghton, where they reflected on the progression from record reseller to label, obscure Japanese ambient, and rental price-outs in Manchester city centre.  

One wise response for a business during a rent crisis is to invent a model that doesn’t need a static location. Vin de Bodega did that, and brought with them a pop-up model for wine selling that allows them to remain mobile and fluid. That way, they can spend all their rental money on Drama Call hoodies and afford more expensive wine. Eve Johnstone chat to them about what they’re doing, the Natural Wine world itself, and then placed it into a broader context with Isca, a small plates restaurant and wine bar based in Levenshulme and Stockport.  

And lastly, two stellar interviews: one with Karim Zeroual, Manny-based, Freemount-frequenting legend, and then an extensive look at the photography of Jay Johnson, whose work you’ll recognise from Drama Call and Clints, where his overt fashion photography shines. Later on you’ll see that Jay’s photography also extends into far more subtle and nuanced domains.  

It’s important for us, as we turn 40, to really get to grips with the area that made Proper Proper. We hope that in this small selection of what the city has to offer, we can at least make a tiny scratch on the surface of Manchester’s creative output, and do justice to the youth scene which Proper - hopefully, anyway - never really left.

title: Hikerdelic x Psychi Boulder Brush Wood
body_html:
The perfect brush for bouldering or big wall pursuits.

Its angular-shaped brush head has been specifically designed to allow for efficient brushing of awkward pockets and blocked crimps, whilst its larger-than-average size means that even the widest of slopers are clean in no time. A true all-rounder.

 

  • Signature Psychi boar hair bristles, sourced as a byproduct of the meat industry.
  • Sturdy & biodegradable wooden handle.
  • Rear loop for carabiner.

title: Hikerdelic x Psychi Bouldering Bucket Burnt Orange / Brown
body_html:
In the creation of our Bouldering Bucket, we wanted to fuse Psychi's climbing know-how with our historical knowledge of traditional outdoor garments, meaning it didn't take us long to settle on its corduroy construction.

What we didn't anticipate was how good corduroy looks when it's coated in chalk - out of the box this chalk bag is good, but trust us, it looks even better after a few sweaty sessions.

Exclusive Hikerdelic x Psychi branding can be seen on the front of the chalk bag, with our Sporeswear logo making an appearance on the rear.

  • Hardwearing corduroy fabric construction.
  • Spiral closure prevents spillages.
  • Chalk brush loop.
  • Large zip chalk brush stow pocket.
  • Large open stow pocket.
  • Embroidered Hikerdelic x Psychi branding.
  • Embroidered Hikerdelic Sporeswear logo.

title: Hikerdelic x Psychi Shoe Bag Black / Purple
body_html:
It's no secret that climbing shoes can get a bit dirty, constantly cramping your bare feet into incredibly small footwear and then dancing around on chalky polyurethane comes with its own specific smells and debris.

To combat these issues, it's a good idea to confine your shoes to their own specific bag. The Hikerdelic x Psychi Shoe Bag is constructed of a hardwearing black mesh material to hide marks and allow your shoes to breathe.

 

  • Black mesh construction.
  • Hikerdelic Sporeswear x Psychi printed branding.
  • Drawstring closure.
  • Hardwearing canvas base.

title: Proper Magazine Issue 46 - Puma Cover
body_html:
Here we present Proper Magazine 46, an issue that places its focus on the season at hand - autumn.

That landmark issue 50 is well in sight now, but before getting too excited about that, let's return our attention to all the good stuff in this release, of which we believe there's a very healthy smattering. In this issue we celebrate many things - Belstaff's century birthday, the release of KEEN's Jasper Zionic, historical British outdoor clobber, the return of the Puma King, and of course, a whole host of other stuff we're well into.

You can't beat having a physical copy of something, and it must be said, this issue smells almost as good as it looks.

title: Proper Magazine Issue 44 - Goldwin Cover
body_html:
New season, new magazine. This issue is full to the brim with interviews, insight and other things not necessarily beginning with the letter 'i'.

We go for a run with Japanese brand Goldwin, we look at one of Puma's most iconic shoes, we speak to Indonesia's coolest hiking brand, we talk to Lorenzo Osti about the new Massimo Osti Studio project, we get the inside track on the new Magnetic book which documents Osti's work in the pre-internet years, and we also get a look at Gramicci's new And Wander collab.

Oh and we took some pairs of KEEN UNEEK to Todmorden for a look around a cool house in a cool town. Wes Anderson vibes. 

Loads more, as usual.

There are four covers available. The one you're buying is the one shown.

title: Proper Magazine Issue 43 - CAT Cover
body_html:
During the creation of issue 43, we were feeling a bit fragile, it was the first time we'd pledged to do three magazines a year and we were feeling it. In an effort to comfort ourselves, we channelled themes of cosiness.
In this issue, we chat with Universal Works founder David Keyte, talk favourite fives, profess our love for gloves and of course, indulge ourselves heavily in lots of nice jackets and trainers.

title: Hikerdelic Tote Bag Black
body_html: The phrase Tote Bag might conjure up images of lovely cotton shopping bags carried by those girls you see in nicer trainers than you wear. And that's great. We sell them too. But this... well to call it a Tote Bag is to do it a disservice. It's more than that. Sure, it functions as a Tote Bag, but the weight, construction and attention to detail makes it a must have for your trip, whether it's to the local shop for some mint Aeros or on the beach as you grasp at the last of sunshine.
